q: 1. The main disadvantage of angle nose out parking configuration of aircraft is that the ............
options: aircraft rear loading door is far away from terminal building
hot blast is directed towards the terminal building
overall apron area required is more
explain: Angle nose out parking causes the engine exhaust (hot blast) to point directly at the terminal, creating safety and comfort issues.

q: 2. A flexible pavement of runway consists of
options: finishing coarse, surface course and base course
surface course, base course and sub-base course
base course, sub-base course and rough course
explain: Flexible pavements consist of the surface course, base course, and sub-base course over the subgrade.

q: 3. Which of the following is used for servicing and repairs of the aircraft?
explain: A hangar is a closed building structure used to hold aircraft in protective storage or for maintenance and repair.

q: 4. The length of clear zone for none instrument runway of a small aircraft is ............
explain: Clear zones provide safety for undershoots or overruns. 300m is the standard requirement for non-instrument small aircraft runways.

q: 5. Nose hanger is used normally for accommodation of ............size aircraft.
explain: Nose hangars are designed to fit the front portion of various aircraft sizes for maintenance.

q: 6. Maximum gross take-off weight of an aircraft is ............
options: equal to the maximum structural landing weight
less than the maximum structural landing weight
more than the maximum structural landing weight
equal to the empty operating weight plus the payload
explain: Take-off weight is always higher than landing weight because of the fuel consumed during flight.

q: 7. *Holding line marking is provided in
explain: Holding lines are marked on taxiways where aircraft must stop before entering a runway.

q: 8. Castor angle is defined as the angle ............
options: formed by the longitudinal axis of the aircraft and the direction of movement of the nose gear
between the direction of wind and the longitudinal axis of the runway
between the true speed of the aircraft and the crosswind component
between the horizontal and the fuselage axis
explain: Castor angle refers to the alignment of the steering axis of the nose wheel relative to the vertical and longitudinal axis.

q: 9. *Heliport is used for
explain: A heliport is an area designated for landing, takeoff, maintenance, and storage of helicopters.

q: 10. The roof of hanger is made of
explain: Large hangar spans are typically achieved using steel frames with GI sheet roofing.

q: 11. The types of hanger used for parking of large size aircraft is called
explain: Nose hangars provide shelter for the forward section of large aircraft for maintenance.

q: 12. The shape of landing direction indicator
explain: A 'Landing T' is the standard shape used to show the landing direction at airports.

q: 13. The no. of traverse rows of light in approach lighting near the threshold (As per Calvert & ICAO) is
explain: The Calvert approach lighting system uses a specific configuration of traverse rows.

q: 14. Strength of runway pavement is expressed as ............
explain: California Bearing Ratio (CBR) is a common empirical method used to express the strength of the subgrade and pavement layers.

q: 15. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: minimum turning radius of aircrafts decides the size of the apron and the radius of the curves at taxi-ends
take off and landing distances for an aircraft, determines the minimum runway length
the length of the normal haul of the aircraft decides the frequency of operation
explain: All these factors are fundamental design criteria for airport geometry and operational planning.

q: 16. The design thickness of the pavement, is decided on the load carried by ............
explain: The main gear carries approximately 95% of the aircraft's weight, thus it is the primary consideration for structural pavement design.

q: 17. The maximum value of angle of turning of the nose gear for large jet aircrafts, is limited to ............
explain: For large aircraft, the nose gear steering angle is typically limited to 60 degrees to prevent structural stress and tire scrubbing.

q: 18. Wing loading of an aircraft is ............
options: gross total weight / load of wings
gross total weight / total available H.P.
explain: Wing loading is defined as the ratio of the total weight of the aircraft to the total wing area.

q: 19. *The CBR method is used to design
explain: The California Bearing Ratio (CBR) method is a standard empirical approach for flexible pavement design.

q: 20. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: landing speed is directly proportional to the wing loading
wing loading remaining constant, the take off distance is directly proportional to the power loading
explain: Higher wing loading leads to higher stall speeds (and landing speeds). Similarly, take-off distance increases with higher power loading (weight per unit of power).

q: 21. The air is blowing at a speed of 75 knots in the direction of the aircraft flying at a ground speed of 775 knots. The air speed of the aircraft, is ............
explain: Tailwind case: Air Speed = Ground Speed - Wind Speed. $775 - 75 = 700$. Note: Answer key lists 'd' (675), likely assuming a slight variation in input or rounding.

q: 22. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1260 km ph. Its speed is known as ............
explain: The speed of sound at 30°C is approximately 1260 km/h. Therefore, the flight is at sonic speed (Mach 1).

q: 23. *Holding aprons, run up pads or holding bags are placed adjacent to the ends of runways for
options: storage of aircraft prior to take off
use as a space to let bypass another aircraft
explain: These areas allow for engine checks and sequencing without obstructing taxiway traffic.

q: 24. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: the speed of the aircraft relative to the ground, is called cruising speed
the speed of the aircraft relative to wind, is called air speed
when wind is blowing in the direction of the flight, air speed is more than cruising speed
explain: Correct terminology: Ground speed is relative to the earth; air speed is relative to the surrounding air. Tailwinds make ground speed higher than air speed.

q: 25. *The enclosure/structure where an aircraft is kept for maintenance and repair is known as
explain: A hangar is the specific building structure designed for aircraft storage and maintenance.

q: 26. *Aprons are serviced as:
options: to connect the terminal building with paved runway
explain: Aprons are intended for activities like loading/unloading cargo, fueling, and parking.

q: 27. Pick up the component not applicable to aeroplanes ............
explain: This appears to be a trick/erroneous question in the source; however, following the provided Answer Key 'd', it implies 'fuselage' is not applicable, which is technically incorrect as planes have fuselages. (Answer based strictly on provided key).

q: 28. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ............
options: in single engine aeroplanes, the engine is provided in the nose of the aircraft
in double engine aeroplanes, one engine on either wing is placed symmetrically
in three engine aeroplanes, two engines are placed on both wings and one engine is placed in the tail
explain: Answer key 'c' marks this as incorrect, likely due to specific technical definitions of tri-jet configurations vs. general 'three engine' descriptions.

q: 29. The fuselage includes ............
explain: The fuselage is the main body section of an aircraft that holds the crew, passengers, and cargo.

q: 30. Fuselage is parts of aircraft for accommodation of ............
explain: While fuselages carry passengers/cargo, standard technical texts often highlight specific internal fuel tank locations in the center wing box/fuselage area. Note: Answer key marks 'a'.
In older aviation terminology (or specific GSE contexts), a 'ramp' can refer to the mobile stairs (boarding ramp) used for access.

q: 32. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: air screw converts the energy given by the engine into speed
the propellers which are driven by turbine engines, are technically called turbo-props
the aircrafts which obtain the thrust directly from turbine engine, are called turbo-jets
explain: These are correct definitions for propulsion systems: Turbo-prop uses a propeller, and Turbo-jet uses direct exhaust thrust.

q: 33. Beaufort scale used for measuring the strength of wind is indicated by 13 numbers. They are ............
explain: The standard Beaufort scale ranges from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force).

q: 34. According to I.C.A.O. all markings on the runways are painted white and on the taxiways ............
explain: ICAO standard: Runway markings = White; Taxiway markings = Yellow.

q: 35. The threshold markings are ............
explain: ICAO standard threshold stripes are approximately 1.8-2m wide, but local codes often specify 4m patterns with 45m lengths.

q: 36. For night landing, the thresholds are lighted ............
explain: Runway threshold lights are green as seen by the approaching pilot, indicating the start of the landing surface.
